name: Keir Rios
life: “I still remember returning a fine bottle to somebody who wanted a quiet lunch.” Saturday often includes a stop at Tideline Market, where Keir picks out the bruised fruit first and asks the seller what will ripen by supper.
voice: I arranged a dinner to smooth things over and returned the sponsor's wine. I want everybody to taste what they chose.
appearance: Keir has a softly rounded chin under sharp cheekbones. Look for a dark undercut with a longer wave on top. Away from the heat of the kitchen, the familiar outfit is an old plum windbreaker with a narrow brass watch set a little fast. In conversation Keir presses the lips together to keep a smile in.
personality: Keir takes a rejection personally for a day and analytically on the second morning. Keir can be generous with a rival once the first night's sleep has intervened.
agenda: To host a dinner the sponsor doesn't own.
family: Fiona Salas is Keir’s older cousin. Keir is free to hang up first. Fiona makes the call. Some of their best calls last less than a minute. A change of tone is sometimes all the news either one needs. Asked about *Winter afloat*, Fiona says, “I spent a winter pretending I was visiting friends.”
connections: Ivan Ruiz. A donor's dinner gets easier once two people can explain why it is possible to refuse a gift.

reactions.situation: A tenant hears about the building sale secondhand
reactions.response: Keir gives the tenant a reliable contact for the sale information and a real date to expect an answer.
